summary.headline: Jindal Supreme Q2 FY27 revenue rose 36% YoY to INR216.22 crore and EBITDA rose 122% to INR16.94 crore, with EBITDA margin at 7.8%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 36% YoY to INR216.22 crore, with EBITDA up 122% to INR16.94 crore and margin expanding to 7.8% from 4.8%. H1 FY27 PAT rose 72% to INR18.19 crore on 23% revenue growth, which management called its strongest half-year. Margin gains were attributed to a higher value-added mix (57.5%), capacity utilisation up to 65.46% from 61.6%, and fixed-cost absorption. Balance sheet deleveraged after the IPO fresh issue, with debt-to-equity at 0.48x, though working capital days rose to 64 from 57 and H1 operating cash flow was negative.

financial_highlights.change: +36% YoY vs INR158.84 crore in Q2 FY26
vs 1.2x in FY26 and 2.1x in FY24

segments.name: Black pipes
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation about 70% in H1 FY27, the highest of the main categories.

segments.name: GI (galvanised) pipes
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation about 65% in H1 FY27; galvanising capacity raised to 63,000 tons with the new 18,000-ton line.

segments.name: Metal beam crash barriers
segments.commentary: Utilisation about 56% in H1 FY27; capacity doubled to 48,000 tons from 24,000 tons after new line reached commercial operation.

segments.name: GI tubular poles
segments.commentary: New line started April 2025; utilisation about 45% in H1 FY27, with management targeting 80-85% by Q4 FY27 and cited as key H1 growth driver.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at INR850-900 crore; management said H2 will be much stronger than H1.
FY27 EBITDA guided at around INR60-odd crore for the full year.
Capacity utilisation path: about 70% in Q3 FY27, 75% in Q4 FY27, and 80% around Q1 FY28; poles targeted at 80-85%.
Double-digit EBITDA margin expected only once utilisation reaches about 80%, by roughly Q1 FY28; 7-8% described as the bottom-case, sustainable level.
Working capital days targeted at 45-50 (also cited as 45-55) from 64, to be reached in H2 FY27.
Value-added mix targeted to rise from about 65% to 70-75%.
capex_capacity: Total installed capacity about 171,000 tons per annum; around 200,000 tons expected by end FY27 with the added galvanising line and solar structures.
Galvanising line 5 (about 24,000 tons per annum) under capex, expected operational around Q2 FY28 per one answer and Q4 FY28 per prepared remarks.
Nut and bolts manufacturing introduction targeted for Q4 FY27; excluded from the 200,000-ton figure because tonnage is small though value is high.
Solar structures to enter production by Q4 FY27.

Greenfield plant in Raipur, Chhattisgarh: about 75-80 acres under acquisition, closing expected in Q4 FY27; Phase 1 capex about INR150 crore for about 150,000 tons per annum, targeted for commissioning by March 2028; full potential up to about INR600 crore phased, about 4x Hisar footprint.
Phase 2 at the greenfield site to start once Phase 1 reaches about 50% utilisation; Phase 1 funding split roughly 50:50 between internal accruals and debt.
demand_pricing: Government schemes cited as demand drivers: Jal Jeevan Mission, AMRUT, Smart Cities, dedicated freight corridors and bullet train projects.
Indian pipes and tubes industry expected to grow 7-8% CAGR to about USD 24 billion by 2036 (per management).
Pricing: management said steel cost changes are passed through with about a 2-week lag as a re-roller.
No single customer above 5% of revenue; dealers contribute about 20% of revenue (50+ active dealers, up from 34 previously).
Remaining roughly 80% of revenue is direct: about 30% EPC players, about 30% crash barrier buyers (NHAI contractors, BSNL, ITI, Delhi Buildcon, NCC), balance pipes.
No order book for pipes (day-to-day orders); poles carry about one month's order book.
Crash barriers sold on 100% advance payment; pole sales to EPC companies backed by letters of credit; debtor days about 12-13.
Northern India focus (Delhi NCR, Rajasthan, Punjab, Himachal, J&K); Haryana about 25% of revenue; crash barriers also sold to Maharashtra, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh.

qa_highlights.question: Opportunity in GI tubular poles and timeline for utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Poles target hilly areas for streetlights and telecom towers; utilisation expected at 80-85% within about three years, reaching 80-85% by Q4 FY27 from about 45% now.

qa_highlights.question: Why net working capital rose to 64 days from 57, and the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory was built up to take advantage of higher steel prices; target is 45-50 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why H1 operating cash flow was negative (about INR6-7 crore) despite PAT of about INR18 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory build-up and receivables rising to INR42 crore from INR33 crore a year earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Reconcile INR71 crore debt repayment with a borrowing decline of about INR30 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Short-term borrowings fell because inventory was run down from INR115 crore to INR100 crore; long-term debt repayment to show in later periods.

qa_highlights.question: Greenfield plans, capex and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Chhattisgarh (Raipur) site of 75-80 acres; Phase 1 about INR150 crore funded roughly 50:50 between internal accruals and debt; no equity dilution planned currently.

qa_highlights.question: H1 vs H2 sales split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 40:60 split, with H2 much stronger due to added capacity in crash barriers and poles.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity at year-end and FY28 volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: About 200,000 tons by end FY27; FY28 output expected at 15,000-16,000 tons per month, about 170,000-180,000 tons.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new galvanising unit commercial and when will it contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Commercial production achieved end October; expected to add meaningful volume from December.

risks_watch: Working capital and cash conversion: NWC at 64 days and negative H1 operating cash flow; the 45-50 day target must be delivered in H2.
Other current assets rose to about INR40 crore from about INR15 crore in H1, partly IPO expense, expected to reverse in H2 when IPO costs are adjusted against reserves.
Execution on utilisation ramp (70% Q3, 75% Q4, 80% Q1 FY28) and on new lines (nut and bolts, solar structures, galvanising line 5).
Greenfield Chhattisgarh land closing (Q4 FY27) and commissioning by March 2028, a tight timeline management described as roughly one year to build; funding includes new debt.
Margin sensitivity: fixed-cost absorption supports margin, but steel price swings are passed through with a 2-week lag.
Dealer count strategy: management intends to grow sales per dealer rather than add dealers.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, margins and deleveraging, with specific numeric targets for utilisation, working capital and FY27 guidance. Less precise on some balance-sheet and product-mix questions, where answers were corrected or deferred (e.g., EBITDA-per-ton composition, debt reconciliation, other current assets).
key_quotes: Our EBITDA per ton has improved significantly from, INR2,100 per ton to INR5,800 per ton in H1 of FY27.
What we are doing right now is absolutely the bottom case scenario for us, this 7% to 8% EBITDA is very much doable over a much longer term also.
Instead of increasing more number of dealers, we would be focusing more on increasing the sales per dealer.

adds.what: 5th galvanising line, about 24,000 tons per annum (under capex)
Greenfield Raipur plant Phase 1, about 150,000 tons per annum

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at INR850-900 crore (about 21% growth on the implied base of roughly INR700-750 crore, which is the midpoint), with H2 much stronger than H1 and utilisation rising from 65.5% to about 80% by Q1 FY28; backing is partly specific (utilisation path, 18,000-ton GI line and 48,000-ton crash barrier doubling already live, 5th galvanising line and Raipur Phase 1 timelines) but H2 ramp

quality.why: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 36% YoY to INR216.22 crore, with margin gains attributed to a higher value-added mix (57.5%), utilisation rising to 65.46% from 61.6%, and fixed-cost absorption, but the brief gives no revenue split between volume and price for the quarter and names no one-off items for either the quarter or the year-ago base.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management says double-digit EBITDA margin only once utilisation reaches about 80% (roughly Q1 FY28), up from 65.5% now and 7.8% in Q2 FY27; 7-8% is the bottom-case level, and value-added mix is targeted to rise from about 65% to 70-75%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Galvanising line (18,000 tons) and crash barrier doubling to 48,000 tons are already live, nut and bolts and solar structures are due Q4 FY27, and installed capacity is set to reach about 200,000 tons by end FY27 from about 171,000 tons now.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided at INR850-900 crore vs an implied base of about INR700-750 crore (about 21% growth), with H2 at roughly 60% of sales and utilisation rising from 65.5% to about 80% by Q1 FY28.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Raipur greenfield land (75-80 acres) closes in Q4 FY27 with Phase 1 capex of about INR150 crore for 150,000 tons, and 5th galvanising line (24,000 tons) is already under capex; utilisation is about 65% so further capex is also needed beyond that.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance of INR850-900 crore revenue and about INR60 crore EBITDA is new and leans on a steep H2 ramp (H2 about 60% of sales), so an upgrade depends on the utilisation path holding.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The H2 ramp needs utilisation from 65.5% to 70%, 75% and 80% by Q1 FY28, and the 45-50 day working capital target must be delivered from 64 days; poles at about 45% utilisation and crash barriers at about 56% are the weakest lines.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Nut and bolts introduction and solar structure production are both targeted for Q4 FY27, although nut and bolts tonnage is small.

rows.label: Working capital days cut to 45-50 from 64
rows.why: NWC at 64 days vs 57 in FY26 after inventory build; management targets 45-50 days in H2 FY27, with inventory already run down from INR115 crore to INR100 crore.

rows.label: Galvanising line 5 (24,000 tons) and Raipur Phase 1 commissioning
rows.why: 5th galvanising line is under capex and expected around Q2 FY28 (or Q4 FY28 per prepared remarks); Raipur Phase 1 (150,000 tons) is targeted for March 2028, which is a tight timeline.

rows.label: Debt-to-equity down to 0.48x from 1.2x in FY26
rows.why: Post-IPO fresh issue cut D/E from 1.2x in FY26 to 0.48x, but Phase 1 Raipur capex (about INR150 crore, 50:50 debt and internal accruals) adds new debt.

tone.note: Management was confident on utilisation ramp, margins and FY27 guidance, and on deleveraging; it was less precise on working capital, the H1 cash flow shortfall, other current assets and the debt reconciliation, which were corrected or deferred.
